task_instance: Run a compliance check on launching a cash-reward customer referral program (referrer gets $25 via PayPal/bank transfer per new paying customer referred, US + EU, collecting referrer name/email/payment details and referred friend's name/email), producing the skill's standard markdown compliance-check report (summary, applicable regulations table, requirements table, risk areas table, recommended actions, approvals needed, further review recommended).
evidence: Read SKILL.md to get the required output template and its built-in Privacy Regulation Overview (GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, other regs) and DPA checklist content. Created scenario.md describing a concrete referral-program initiative and data flows. Wrote compliance-check-output.md following the exact template structure from SKILL.md (Summary; Applicable Regulations and Policies table covering GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, FTC Endorsement Guides, CAN-SPAM/TCPA, state referral statutes, payment/AML rules, international transfers; Requirements table with 8 items and status/action; Risk Areas table with severity/mitigation; 5 Recommended Actions; Approvals Needed table naming Legal/Marketing Compliance/Finance/Security/DPO; Further Review Recommended section), plus a closing disclaimer matching the skill's 'not legal advice' requirement. Verified the deliverable by reading the written file back and confirming all required template sections are present and populated with substantive, scenario-specific content. Both files were written directly (no shell/mkdir used) to the work directory: scenario.md and compliance-check-output.md, alongside this result.json. No blockers were encountered because the skill's core deliverable is a text/markdown report, which is fully within the office-assistant runtime's read/write/edit text-file capability -- no code execution, binary file production, or connector/MCP access was needed.
